schema_note: Short, dated, sourced 'recent developments' items shown in the bottom-right box of each commentary section on country.html -- see getDevelopments.js/setDevelopments.js. One array per commentary section key. This is a pilot for the UK, added 2026-07-29 alongside the new two-column commentary layout, before deciding on a full 33-country rollout or refresh cadence.

wealth.headline: Cash ISA allowance to be cut to £12,000 from April 2027
wealth.summary: Stocks & Shares and Innovative Finance ISA limits stay at £20,000; only the cash allowance is reduced, an explicit government push to tilt retail savings toward market investment.

wealth.headline: Savers increasingly treating ISAs and pensions as complementary, not competing
wealth.summary: With pension savings now inside the inheritance tax net, retirement planners report a shift toward holding both wrappers deliberately -- pensions for tax-efficient growth, ISAs for accessible income -- rather than defaulting to one over the other.

pensions.headline: DWP opens consultation on DB surplus release conditions
pensions.summary: Around four in five DB schemes are now in surplus, with an aggregate surplus estimated at roughly £160bn. The consultation on draft regulations (open until 2 September 2026) follows the Pension Schemes Act 2026 (royal assent April 2026), which eased the path to releasing that surplus to employers; rules are expected in force from April 2027. Builds directly on the Chancellor's Mansion House 'megafund' agenda.

pensions.headline: LGPS pooling deadline passes with several pools still incomplete
pensions.summary: The 31 March 2026 deadline was meant to consolidate £274bn of assets from 86 administering authorities into six FCA-authorised pools. Government has since relaxed some FCA-authorisation requirements after the deadline slipped; Wales Pension Partnership and Northern LGPS still lack FCA authorisation. LGPS Central alone now oversees roughly £100bn after adding six new partner funds (Gloucestershire, Hampshire, Norfolk, Oxfordshire, Suffolk, Wiltshire).

insurance.headline: Bulk annuity market on track for another record year
insurance.summary: LCP forecasts £40-55bn of buy-ins in 2026, up from £38bn in 2025; WTW sees total risk transfer (buy-ins, buyouts and longevity swaps combined) exceeding £70bn. Buyout has cemented itself as the default DB scheme endgame ahead of run-on.

insurance.headline: M&A wave reshapes the bulk annuity insurer landscape
insurance.summary: Athora's acquisition of Pension Insurance Corporation cleared regulatory approval on 6 March 2026; Brookfield Wealth Solutions completed its acquisition of Just Group on 1 April 2026; JAB's acquisition of Utmost is expected to follow later in the year. Consolidates specialist bulk annuity balance sheets into fewer, larger, increasingly private-capital-backed owners.

charities.headline: Women's Resource Centre launches UK's first women's-charity endowment fund
charities.summary: The Women's Forever Fund aims to secure £350m over six years, invested ethically as a permanent endowment, to unlock over £20m of grantmaking for women's charities over that period.

foundations.headline: Six foundations launch the 2026 Endowments Investing Challenge
foundations.summary: Joseph Rowntree Foundation, Vivensa Foundation and Children's Society Foundation are among six foundations committing up to £50m combined to invest endowment capital for social and environmental impact, advised by a panel of 18-25 year-olds (the Future Generations Panel).

foundations.headline: UK's largest 300 endowed foundations hold £84bn, mostly unscreened for impact
foundations.summary: The bulk of this capital remains invested in mainstream capital markets without regard to the social or environmental goals of the foundations that hold it -- a persistent gap between mission and investment policy that's increasingly being raised with trustees.

family_offices.headline: UK family office footprint keeps widening despite London cost pressures
family_offices.summary: London remains a leading family-office hub, but rising costs are pushing some newer offices toward multi-jurisdiction structures. The UK market was valued at roughly $5.2bn in 2024 and is projected to grow at a 6.7% CAGR to around $9.9bn by 2034, with a growing share of offices moving into impact investing.

sovereign_wealth_funds.headline: National Wealth Fund commits £5.8bn across ten strategic sectors
sovereign_wealth_funds.summary: Part of its stated ambition to catalyse more than £100bn of total investment into UK companies, infrastructure and supply chains and support over 200,000 jobs. The £5.8bn spans ten sectors including hydrogen and carbon capture.
sovereign_wealth_funds.source: Fuel Cells Works / National Wealth Fund

sovereign_wealth_funds.headline: National Wealth Fund signs a run of large co-investment deals
sovereign_wealth_funds.summary: Recent commitments include up to £500m with Lloyds Banking Group for university estate decarbonisation, £200m to Associated British Ports' infrastructure programme, and a £500m battery storage platform (Eelpower Energy) alongside Equitix and Aware Super -- illustrating the Fund's growing role as a co-investment partner for institutional capital.

ocio.headline: Global OCIO assets near $3.3tn, forecast to reach $5.6tn by 2029 (global figure, not UK-specific)
ocio.summary: Cited here as backdrop rather than a UK data point -- no UK-specific OCIO market sizing was found in this pass. Relevant as more UK family offices and smaller institutions look to outsource CIO functions rather than build in-house teams; worth revisiting once UK-specific figures surface.
